what: 0.2.4: three products of a several-conversation verify step off few-workgroup kernels (apply_verify_small_products); and what did not pay: an expert-grouped MoE kernel, a one-pass 9-16 column Q8_0 kernel, the short-row copy path
setup: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-IQ4_XS, the manager's profile with parallel=4, ctx 262144, f16 K/V, MTP with draft_max 3 and the cap 3,2,2,2,0. tmp/kvr/bs_probe.py / bs_sweep.py on a server started as production (tmp/kvr/with_server.py): N conversations of distinct real text (~4K tokens each) pinned to slots and cached first. Development A/Bs: greedy, 256 tokens a stream, the verify step's median time per pass from STRIX_SPEC_TIMING=1 (the 'decode' column of tmp/kvr/st_summary.py), each configuration on a fresh server, alternating in the same run.

changes.concat: the GDN conv input ggml_concat(state, transpose(x), 0) of 2-31 tokens per sequence took concat_non_cont: one 256-thread block per channel and sequence for 3 + tokens values, ~30K blocks at three conversations; now the tiled transpose from 2 tokens (STRIX_CONCAT_T_MIN, was 32). A copy either way, so a single conversation's output is bit for bit 0.2.3's
changes.bf16_chunks: the indexer's BF16 k projection [2560 x 128] at 9-32 columns took MMB's one 128-row tile (one workgroup); BF16 weights now take the vector kernel over column chunks there (STRIX_BF16_VEC_CHUNK_MAX, 32)
changes.q_chunks: quantized weights of at most 1024 output rows at 9-32 columns (hyper-connection down [10240 -> 320] x96 a step, attention k / v, shared expert gate / up) took 3-5 MMQ tiles, no stream-k on RDNA; now the vector kernel over 8-column chunks (STRIX_Q_VEC_CHUNK_MAX 32, STRIX_Q_VEC_CHUNK_ROWS 1024). With 2560 rows ([6144 -> 2560]) the chunks were slower than MMQ, so they stay

4 streams.note: one 0.2.4 run at 130.1 had every host column raised too (process, sample, other) and is left out

1 stream.note: the cleanest pair (tmp/kvr/dev_iso.sh); other pairs spread +/-2 ms both ways

release_ab.reading: a round's tok/s follows the acceptance of the text it sampled (54-86% here, ~0.4-0.5 tok/s a point); the builds' mean acceptance differs by chance in both directions (three: 71.3 against 64.7, four: 65.4 against 68.6), so they are compared at the same acceptance. Every completed round is kept (0.2.3's at 54% too); one round failed, 0.2.3's first at four streams (HTTP 500: ignore_eos ran a text past its end into template tags, which the server's output parser rejects; a probe artifact, chats stop at the end)
release_ab.method: 0.2.3 against 0.2.4, alternating, three passes of three rounds, 3 / 4 streams, 512 tokens a stream, ~4K tokens each, default sampling with a new seed every round and pass (the same seeds for both builds; tmp/kvr/rel024_ab2.sh)

release_ab_fixed_seeds.method: 0.2.3 as released (tmp/rt023) against the 0.2.4 build, alternating, three passes of two rounds, 1 / 3 / 4 streams, 512 tokens a stream, ~4K tokens each, the server's default sampling with the seed fixed per stream (tmp/kvr/rel024_ab.sh)

step_medians.note: passes 2 and 3 (the logs of pass 1 were overwritten before they were kept); n=4 here is mostly one conversation (1 x 4 tokens), as four conversations drafted most steps

release_ab_fixed_seeds.reading: misleading: with a fixed seed a server that computes every step the same way samples the same text every round, and the acceptance is that text's. 0.2.4 did (67% in 5 of 6 rounds at three), 0.2.3 did not (65-79%), so this compared about one text of 0.2.4 with three of 0.2.3; see determinism

one_conversation_varied_seeds.method: 0.2.4, one stream, the A/B's seeds (three seed bases of three rounds, tmp/kvr/one_024.sh), 512 tokens, ~4K tokens
one_conversation_varied_seeds.reading: for the README's 'x one conversation': 3 streams 53.6 / 35.8 = 1.50x, 4 streams 61.4 / 35.8 = 1.71x (0.2.4's plain means). One conversation drafts 3 tokens (lower acceptance per token than the 2 of several)

determinism.method: three streams, four rounds, the seed fixed per stream, a sha1 prefix of each stream's text per round (tmp/kvr/acc_ab.sh): 0.2.4, the 0.2.4 build with STRIX_BF16_VEC_CHUNK_MAX=0 STRIX_Q_VEC_CHUNK_MAX=0 STRIX_CONCAT_T_MIN=32 (0.2.3's routing), 0.2.3
determinism.reading: 0.2.4 sampled the same three texts in all four rounds; with 0.2.3's routing the build gave 0.2.3's texts (3761d9 d57253 4a2d75, 72%) in three rounds and another in the fourth; 0.2.3 gave three different outcomes in four rounds. Which text is sampled decides the acceptance. The run-to-run differences come from steps that carry a different number of tokens (the conversations do not always join the same step): up to 0.2.3 these products took the vector kernel at 1-8 tokens and MMQ / MMB from 9, so a token's result could depend on the step it landed in; 0.2.4 keeps them on the vector kernel up to 32 tokens. Four conversations still vary (the taller weights still change kernel at 9)

ppl_ubatch16.method: tmp/kvr/ppl_kb.py, ctx 4096, 2 chunks, ubatch 16 (every batch takes the new paths), f16 K/V, the 0.2.4 build
ppl_ubatch16.reading: no accuracy lost on the new paths (the 8K / 8-chunk gate is 2.6814 on both, its batches are 8192 tokens)

not_kept.expert_grouped_kernel: a MoE vector kernel reading each distinct expert once for all its tokens: real verify steps share experts a lot (9 tokens of three conversations: 90 expert-token pairs, 54 distinct experts; 12 tokens: 120, 67; the three tokens of one conversation 28% of their pairs), but the 32 MB MALL already serves the repeats. v1 (a serial scan of the ids in every block) -30%; v2 (a one-block grouping kernel, blocks look it up) neutral (3 streams 98.5 / 98.0 against 99.1 / 99.0 ms). Op tests passed and a single conversation was bit for bit, so it is only parked
not_kept.wide_q8_0_kernel: a one-pass Q8_0 kernel for 9-16 columns (weights read once, the quants loaded once per block for every column): 1.5-3x faster than MMQ in the op bench, where a single weight stays in the MALL, but in the model equal to the chunks above (3 streams 99.2 / 99.9 ms, 4 streams 122.3 / 123.3)
not_kept.short_row_copies: strided copies with rows under 1 KB on the copy kernel instead of hipMemcpy2DAsync (the conv state's rollback-slot copies are 12-byte rows): neutral (3 streams 101.5 / 99.95 against 101.5 / 99.7)

measurement_notes.fixed_seeds: a fixed seed per stream makes every round of a deterministic server one and the same sample: compare builds with a new seed every round (bs_probe.py --vary-seeds) or by the verify step's time
measurement_notes.graph_events: STRIX_GRAPH_EVENTS (an event node before every dispatch of a captured HIP graph): the totals hold after removing ~13.4 us a node, but single dispatches get zero, negative or their neighbour's time, so per-op readings from it misled (a 'dense Q8_0 at 2.5-3x its bandwidth time' that the model did not show)
measurement_notes.op_benches: test-backend-ops with 8 weights a case (bs=8) supplies the parallelism a single weight lacks, and with one weight the MALL holds it: neither shows a single decode-sized product's DRAM behaviour
measurement_notes.leaving_ops_out: dropping a node class (output garbage) collapsed the MoE routing onto a few experts, so the step got faster for the wrong reason (-9 ms for 144 copies that cost ~0 when kept)
measurement_notes.running_ops_twice: running a class twice (same output) gives its cost when the op is idempotent: norms ~0, copies / gathers ~1 ms, flash attention ~1-2 ms of a 100 ms nine-token step; elementwise ops are not (the allocator reuses their inputs in place)
measurement_notes.where_the_step_goes: at nine tokens ~100 ms against a floor of ~51 ms (dense weights 4.6 GB, distinct experts 6 GB): the routed experts run at ~85% of DRAM peak for the distinct experts; the GDN kernel writes one full recurrent state per token for rollback (3 MB a sequence a layer, ~1 GB a step at three conversations); the host leaves the GPU ~3 ms before each verify step (GPU busy ~89%)
